notes: Criminal prosecution for keeping/abetting an assignation (disorderly) house via a service-car driver arranging paid liaisons; concerns prostitution regulation, not lawful lodging/boarding of paying occupants.

Premises-liability suit over an uncovered well in a passageway shared by several tenants; addresses a landlord's duty to maintain retained common areas, not compensated short-term letting of rooms/dwellings.
Fire-insurance vacancy-clause dispute over whether a tenant's temporary absence rendered a dwelling 'vacant or unoccupied'; unrelated to short-term letting or boarding-house regulation.

holding_summary: A business college's written contract reserved the right to require students to board — meaning room as well as meals — at homes the college approved. When a student refused to move from Mrs. Alford's rooming house to another approved rooming house, the college was entitled to bar her from class until she complied, and this did not constitute an unlawful expulsion.

quotes.text: As commonly used, the word “board” means lodging as well as food.
The plain meaning of the stipulation was that appellee was to have the right while appellant attended its school to require her to room, as well as to take her meals, at homes it approved.

notes: polarity left null — the case adjudicates a college's contractual right to direct where a student lodges, not the legality or regulation of the private householders' (Mrs. Alford's, Mrs. Christian's) letting practice itself.

Suit for penalty on a liquor dealer's bond for keeping a disorderly saloon/dance-hall nuisance; the plaintiff's wife's boarders leaving is cited only as evidence of the plaintiff's damages, not an adjudicated lodging arrangement.
Fire-insurance vacancy-clause dispute over whether a substitute occupant's stay kept a dwelling 'occupied'; ordinary uncompensated tenancy-for-owner arrangement, not paid lodging or boarding.

Injunction suit to abate bawdy/disorderly houses and a city ordinance segregating prostitution; concerns regulation of vice and a landlord renting to a bawdy-house operator, not lawful short-term lodging/boarding letting.
School-land forfeiture dispute over a settler's temporary absence while attending normal school; no letting, lodging, or boarding of any kind is at issue.
Dispute over a landlord's statutory distress lien reaching a barber-tenant's exempt tools of trade; a commercial-tenancy exemption question unrelated to residential lodging or boarding.

Constitutional challenge to a zoning ordinance barring retail stores from residential districts; concerns commercial land-use zoning and general property-use rights, not compensated occupancy of another's dwelling/rooms.
Corporate-liability suit over an automobile-rental company's tort liability and charter powers; renting of vehicles, unrelated to letting of dwellings or rooms.
Farm-lease dispute over a covenant of quiet enjoyment breached by a stranger's tortious eviction; ordinary agricultural lease, not lodging/boarding.
Landlord-tenant dispute over attornment following a foreclosure sale of leased land; no lodging or boarding issue present.
Adverse-possession/limitation dispute over pasture land originally used by permission for grazing horses; not a lodging or boarding arrangement.

holding_summary: An elderly homeowner kept two dwelling houses on one urban lot, living in one and renting rooms in both to lodgers as his sole means of support. The court held that renting rooms in this manner did not constitute a 'business' or 'calling' within the constitutional homestead exemption, so the arrangement did not forfeit the property's homestead protection, and reversed for a jury charge that had wrongly treated it as such a business.

quotes.text: That defendant has no occupation, calling or business except the renting of rooms that he had upon said property, two dwelling houses.
It seems clear that the renting of rooms by appellee was not the pursuit of a calling within the meaning of the Constitution.
The renting of rooms in the manner shown by the evidence does not constitute the exercise of a calling or business within the meaning of the Constitution.

notes: Waste/injunction suit over a tenant cutting an opening in a party wall between two adjoining leased commercial buildings; unrelated to residential lodging or boarding.
Forcible-detainer action arising from a failed land-purchase contract; possession was held as a prospective buyer, not as a lodger or boarder, so no landlord-tenant relation existed.

holding_summary: In an aggravated-assault case arising from a rent dispute between a prosecutor and his sister's householder-lodger arrangement, the court held that the evidence showed the sister merely rented rooms to lodgers rather than operating a boarding house. Because Texas's statutory lien on personal property runs in favor of hotel and boarding-house keepers but not lodging-house keepers, she had no such lien over the prosecutor's belongings.

quotes.text: The evidence does not show that she was a boarding-house keeper, but merely rented rooms to lodgers.
Our statute gives a lien on personal property in favor of hotel and boarding-house keepers, but not in favor of lodging-house keepers.

notes: polarity marked mixed — the case recognizes private room-letting to a lodger as an ordinary, legally distinct category from a boarding house, but denies the lodging-house keeper the statutory lien available to boarding houses/hotels.
